//: Contract type-checking, separate from jsconfig.json because Next.js owns
that file and regenerates it (its `ignoreDeprecations` value is not even
accepted by the tsc in this workspace).
`checkJs` is false on purpose: this is an opt-in gate, not a migration.
Files carrying `// @ts-check` are checked; everything else is only parsed
so imports resolve. That lets the API boundary be made safe today without
first fixing every untyped component in the app.
Run with `npm run check-types`. Added for the apprentice app in security pass item 8.
`strict` is deliberately off. Turning it on produced 18 errors on the
first annotated service, 16 of them implicit-any on parameters that have
nothing to do with response shapes. A gate that noisy gets switched off,
and then catches nothing at all. What remains is the failure mode this
exists for — reading a property the API does not return (TS2339) — plus
strictNullChecks for the other half, using a nullable DTO field without
handling null. Tighten once the boundary is fully annotated.
